data.body:
CLOSING EVIDENCE — all six criteria met, with AC4's oracle verified GREEN rather than assumed.

MERGED: Gerrit 1306, commit 550442ae58 on main.

AC4 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED, because its oracle is external and could have disagreed. I deliberately did
NOT close when the change merged: at merge time (18:17:01) the API still reported alerts 81 and 82 as OPEN,
pointing at lines 249/250 — the very lines the fix rewrote. That was stale pre-fix scan data, not a failed
fix, but ticking the box then would have asserted something the stated oracle contradicted. CodeQL SAST
re-scanned automatically at 18:17:22 and completed successfully:
    alert 81  state=fixed  fixed_at=2026-08-03T18:19:50Z  py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization
    alert 82  state=fixed  fixed_at=2026-08-03T18:19:50Z  py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization
    open alerts of ANY rule on the repository: 0
AC5 NO DISMISSAL, NO SUPPRESSION: both alerts read state=fixed with a fixed_at timestamp. A dismissal would
read state=dismissed with a dismissed_reason; neither carries one. The code changed.

AC1 ORIGIN COMPARISON, no substring test against a URL:
  _origin(url) -> (scheme, netloc) via urllib.parse.urlsplit, and both assertions are exact tuple equality:
    assert _origin(model.models[1].base_url) == _origin(_FALLBACK_ENDPOINT)
    assert _origin(model.models[0].base_url) != _origin(_FALLBACK_ENDPOINT)
  The endpoint is single-sourced as _FALLBACK_ENDPOINT so the configured and asserted values cannot drift.
  Three `startswith` occurrences remain in the file and each is legitimate — stated so a future reader does
  not think the ban was half-applied:
    :49  my own docstring explaining WHY a URL must never be prefix-tested
    :282 a DELIBERATE assertion that the replaced prefix form WOULD have accepted the look-alike host
    :429 `ran.startswith("fallback:")` — a MODEL NAME, not a URL; outside the rule's subject
AC2 THE PROPERTY IS STILL PROTECTED — proven by mutation, not by inspection. I neutered the endpoint
  threading in build_fallback_model (endpoints = [None] * len(candidates)), which is precisely the
  regression its own docstring warns about ("strings would bypass rebar's builders entirely and silently
  drop each entry's endpoint"). The test went RED:
    AssertionError: assert ('https', 'api.anthropic.com') == ('https', 'fallback.test')
    At index 1 diff: 'api.anthropic.com' != 'fallback.test'
  The fallback entry had fallen back to the provider default — exactly what the test exists to catch. Note
  the failure is now MORE informative than the prefix check produced, because it names the actual host.
  Restored; 16 passed.
AC3 A PREFIX-SHARING LOOK-ALIKE IS REJECTED:
  test_a_host_that_merely_shares_the_endpoint_prefix_is_not_the_same_origin asserts
  _origin("https://fallback.test.evil.example/v1") != _origin(_FALLBACK_ENDPOINT), AND asserts alongside it
  that look_alike.startswith(_FALLBACK_ENDPOINT) is TRUE — so the test records what the old form would have
  accepted, and the weak form cannot return unnoticed. It also pins the normalisation tolerance that
  `startswith` was reaching for: _origin(endpoint + "/") and _origin(endpoint + "/v1/messages") both compare
  EQUAL to the bare endpoint.
AC6 GATES, by exit code on a clean tree: make lint = 0 · make typecheck = 0 · check_config_reads.py = 0 ·
  gen_env_registry.py --check = 0 · full suite = EXIT 0 with 9515 passed, 41 skipped, 1 xfailed.
  Plus Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 before submit.

ASSESSMENT RECORDED, since CodeQL rated these HIGH and the ADR/audit trail should not overstate them: the
exploitability in context was NIL — a hard-coded constant in a unit test, no untrusted input, nothing
branching on the result but the assertion. The genuine defect was a WEAK ASSERTION: the test meant "this
model was built against that endpoint" and checked "the base_url starts with these bytes", which also passes
for a different host sharing the prefix. Fixing it and clearing the alert were the same change, which is why
dismissal would have traded a real (if minor) test weakness for nothing.
